_comment: Keyword classifier over the enquiry field. Section 8.4 of the brief.
Meta field name:    what_type_of_equipment_are_you_after:   (trailing colon)
HubSpot property:   what_type_of_equipment_are_you_after    (no trailing colon)
The trailing colon survives in the HubSpot LABEL but not the internal name.
Tuned against all 58 real enquiries retrieved on 26 August 2026, kept at
test/fixtures/equipment-enquiries.json. Four defects that only real text
exposed, all now fixed:
1. A bare 'Oven' matched nothing. Six leads said exactly that.
2. 'lpg griller' missed, because a strict word boundary rejects the
'er' suffix on 'grill'. Matching now tolerates s, es, er and ers,
but NOT ing, so 'sinks' still matches 'sink' and 'sinking' does not.
3. A lead asking for eleven in catalogue items plus one range hood was
classified out of catalogue on the range hood alone. Mixed enquiries
are now their own state and count as worth having.
4. 'Kitchen', 'Various' and 'Catering equipment' are answers, not
non answers, but they are not classifiable either. They now sit in
'vague' and are excluded from the in against out share rather than
silently deflating it.
KNOWN CONFLICT, needs a decision. Section 8.4 lists ice makers as NOT
financed, while docs/BUSINESS_OVERVIEW.md lists a catalogue category called
'refrigeration & ice'. The brief is treated as authoritative and ice is out.
This is worth resolving: four of the 58 real enquiries mention ice.

matching._comment: Out of catalogue is evaluated first so 'ice maker' is never swept into refrigeration. Longer keywords win over shorter ones, so 'pizza oven' beats 'oven' and 'ice maker' beats 'ice'.

vague._comment: Hospitality enquiries that are genuine but not specific enough to classify. Counted and reported separately, never folded into in or out.
